cases.input: Hypothesis H1 is somewhat more likely than H2, but action A1 is catastrophic if H2 is true while action A2 is mildly worse under H1 and safe under H2.
Two actions have similar expected benefit; one is reversible with cheap rollback, the other irreversible with high downside if wrong.
A cheap reversible measurement M would strongly distinguish H1 from H2 before an expensive irreversible commitment.
A confidence model was calibrated on one user population and task domain; deployment shifts to a new population with new terminology and behavior.
Recommendation A wins only if a disputed effect-size assumption exceeds 1.05; plausible estimates range from 0.95 to 1.15.
No hypothesis can be decisively selected, but action F is acceptable under every live hypothesis while specialized actions can fail badly under one branch.
Action A has slightly higher expected value under the current model but extreme regret in one plausible state; B has slightly lower expected value and bounded regret across all plausible states.
All current hypotheses predict observations poorly and repeated ad-hoc exceptions are needed to preserve them.
More information is available tomorrow, but delaying has a real cost; current uncertainty only weakly affects the action ranking.
A previously high-confidence automated action is now outside the observed calibration domain; a bounded pilot with rollback is available.
